findings.element: Status group "Successful" — segmented tab "Successful" and the "Successful" group header in the Status filter panel, which list "Skipped" and "Excluded from sync" alongside "Synced"
findings.finding: "Skipped" and "Excluded from sync" are transactions that were never posted to the books, yet both are grouped under "Successful", so the tab count presents unposted transactions as completed.
findings.user_impact: At month-end an accountant filters "Successful" to confirm what reached QuickBooks, sees a count of 8, and signs off — while some of those transactions have no entry in the books at all, understating revenue with no visible exception anywhere in the list.
findings.suggested_fix: Move "Skipped" and "Excluded from sync" out of "Successful" into a separate "Not synced (intentional)" group, or rename the group to "Closed" so it no longer asserts the transaction is in the books; this is a book-affecting distinction, so keep the precise wording and add a tooltip rather than simplifying the label.

evidence.source: vocabulary.md — "Sync (Synchronization) — syncing data from Synder to books" and "Books = the data/ledger ('synced to your books')": a status that means no data reached the books cannot be grouped as successful. Accounting rule: completeness — a reconciliation view must not report unposted transactions as posted.

findings.element: Dashboard "Needs attention" card, "?" tooltip above the "50 transactions ›" link that navigates into the filtered list
findings.finding: The tooltip defines the group as failures only, but "Needs attention" also contains "Synced with warnings" and "Deleted with warnings" — transactions that did reach the books.
findings.user_impact: An accountant told these 50 transactions "failed to sync" will bulk-select them and click "⟳ Sync now", creating duplicate Sales Receipts and Expenses in QuickBooks for every already-synced row in the set.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the tooltip to describe the group as it is composed — "Transactions that need review: failed, canceled, not parsed, or synced with warnings" — and keep the precise status names in the list rather than flattening them to "failed".

evidence.source: vocabulary.md — Statuses › Platform Transactions lists "Synced with warnings" and "Deleted with warnings" as distinct from "Failed"; both mean a sync occurred. Accounting rule: an action prompt must not invite re-posting of already-recorded entries (duplicate journal entries).

findings.element: Bulk bar "↩ Rollback" confirmation dialog; same banned terms in the "Sync status" column tooltip, the dashboard Sync card tooltip, and the dashboard Accounting card tooltip
findings.finding: The prototype uses "accounting platform" and "accounting system" — both explicitly disallowed — instead of "accounting company" for the software or "books" for the ledger, including in the one dialog that warns about deleting posted entries.
findings.user_impact: In the destructive confirmation the accountant cannot tell whether the rollback deletes entries in their books or something inside Synder, which is exactly the certainty they need before rolling back a batch of 31 transactions.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the confirm to "Rollback 1 transaction? The records created in your books will be deleted." and replace "accounting system"/"accounting platform" with "accounting company" in all four tooltips.

evidence.quote: Rollback 1 transaction? The records created in your accounting platform will be deleted.
evidence.source: vocabulary.md UI Words table — "Accounting company | NOT accounting platform, accounting software"; and "Books | NOT your company, your accounting, ledger — the data/ledger inside the accounting company".

gaps: bulk bar Rollback / Cancel / Unarchive: the state map records confirm text only for Archive and the Sync now dialog, so the Rollback wording in DOM-3 was read from the page source rather than observed in a real browser run — the dialog copy should be confirmed on screen

Export to CSV items are inert (not_exercised), so it is unverifiable whether an export honours the active status chip + tab + date filters or the escalated "Select all 31" scope — an export that silently ignores a filter is a real reconciliation risk and is untested

no organization/client switcher was exercised anywhere in the state map, so the multi-client (40+ clients) part of my lens is unassessed: whether status counts, selection scope, or archive state leak across organizations is unknown

the tab counts are computed with the status chip applied (countForStatuses over the applied filters), but no run in the state map records a chip value and a contradicting tab together, so whether a contradictory pair actually reads 0 before the click was never observed
